literal: Gu Xian hung in the northeast, Tai Cu arrayed in the northwest, Rui Bin ranged in the southwest.
idiomatic: Gu Xian hung in the northeast, Tai Cu in the northwest, Rui Bin in the southwest.

literal: All alike were vessels and images in wrong positions, tuning and pitch not in harmony.
idiomatic: Every instrument stood in the wrong place; pitch and tuning did not agree.

literal: There were also fourteen ceremonial bells, frames with heads of beasts, at first not struck; now let them be abolished to follow the correct rule.
idiomatic: Fourteen ceremonial bells on beast-headed frames had never been struck; he now proposed abolishing them to restore proper order.

literal: Your servant now according to the Zhou Rite's Bell-Maker's broad rules and the Stone-Chime-Maker's obtuse-acute method, blows pitch pipes to seek tones, strikes bells to seek sound;
idiomatic: He followed the Zhou Rite's Bell-Maker for dimensions and the Stone-Chime-Maker for angles, blowing pipes to fix pitch and striking bells to test tone.

literal: Cut away the redundant, discuss what is solid and recorded.
idiomatic: He stripped away excess and settled on what the records actually required.

literal: According to the twelve months as twelve palaces.
idiomatic: He aligned the twelve months with twelve palace stations.

literal: Each matched the chronogram position and was hung in its proper place.
idiomatic: Each matched its season and hung where it belonged.

literal: When the monthly tones were complete, they were struck as needed in performance.
idiomatic: Once every month's tone was in place, musicians could strike them as the rite demanded.

literal: Then was obtained the meaning of mutual circulation among palaces, and also the substance of pitch-generating one another.
idiomatic: Thus the bells could cycle through the modes and embody the law by which pitches beget one another.

literal: Now measuring the numbers of bells and chimes, each was fixed at twelve frames.
idiomatic: He fixed the count of bells and stone chimes at twelve frames each.

literal: Approved.
idiomatic: The emperor approved.

literal: At that time gentry and officials all went to watch and listen; none failed to sigh in admiration and return.
idiomatic: Court gentlemen flocked to hear the new arrangement and left sighing in admiration.

literal: Grand Tutor and Director of the Masters of Writing Changsun Chengye was skilled in pitch and excellently praised it again.
idiomatic: Grand Tutor Changsun Chengye, a master of pitch, praised the reform again.

literal: Again followed Emperor Xiaowu into the pass, made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Fufeng.
idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu west, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and was enfeoffed Prince of Fufeng.

literal: Soon supervised the national history.
idiomatic: Soon he supervised the national history.

literal: In succession held posts Minister of Works, concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Guardian.
idiomatic: He rose through Minister of Works, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Guardian.

literal: At that time the Rouran ruler knew Fu well and first asked to see Fu, then sent his daughter.
idiomatic: The Rouran khan knew Fu and insisted on seeing him before sending his daughter.

literal: Thereupon he was sent Fu on the mission.
idiomatic: The court therefore sent Fu on the embassy.

literal: Rouran lord and ministers seeing Fu were all delighted and escorted the empress back in marriage.
idiomatic: Rouran lord and ministers rejoiced at Fu and escorted their queen into Wei marriage.

literal: Fu by nature was quick-witted, loved wine, short in appearance and bald.
idiomatic: Fu was quick-witted, fond of wine, short, and bald.

literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou especially favored him; once in the chamber he set out ten jars of wine, each jar holding more than a bushel, all capped, wishing to tease Fu.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou favored him; once he set ten capped jars in the room, each holding over a bushel, to tease him.

literal: Fu just entering the room, seeing them at once was startled and pleased, saying: "Our brothers are very rude—why break into the royal house and sit facing one another?
idiomatic: Fu entered, feigned shock and delight, and said, "Brothers, how rude—why break into the royal house and sit drinking together?

literal: You should return home early."
idiomatic: Go home at once."

literal: Thereupon he took the wine and left.
idiomatic: He carried off the wine.

literal: Emperor Wen clapped his hands and laughed greatly.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen clapped and laughed.

literal: Later he met wind illness; hands and feet did not follow; mouth could not speak; then with the left hand he drew on the ground characters, begging release from his posts.
idiomatic: Later wind illness left him mute and paralyzed; he wrote on the floor with his left hand, begging to be relieved.

literal: Three memorials were not permitted.
idiomatic: Three memorials were refused.

literal: Transferred to Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor.

literal: Died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: The emperor came in person; the hundred officials went to mourn.
idiomatic: The emperor came in person; officials attended the mourning.

literal: Posthumously Grand Marshal and Director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous name Wenjian.
idiomatic: He was posthumously Grand Marshal and director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous name Wenjian.

literal: Son Duan inherited, post Grand Marshalate Director of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Hua.
idiomatic: His son Duan inherited, becoming director on the grand marshalate staff and inspector of Hua.

literal: By nature coarse and obstinate, he rather looked down on others from his base lands; opinion of the time despised him.
idiomatic: Coarse and proud of his estates, he looked down on others; men of the day despised him.

literal: Younger brother of the Stone Marquis, Jia, young was deep and keen, joy and anger did not show on the face, and also had military stratagem.
idiomatic: Jia, younger brother of the Stone Marquis, was grave and keen from youth; joy and anger never showed, and he had military talent.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen he was made Inspector of Xuzhou, very authoritative and gracious.
idiomatic: At Xiaowen's accession he became inspector of Xuzhou, stern yet merciful.

literal: Later enfeoffed Prince of Guangyang to continue the founding line.
idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangyang to continue the founding house.

literal: When Xiaowen campaigned south he ordered Jia to cut off Junkou.
idiomatic: On Xiaowen's southern campaign he ordered Jia to seal Junkou.

literal: Jia missed the command and let the bandits escape.
idiomatic: Jia missed his orders and let the enemy escape.

literal: The emperor angrily reproached him saying: "Uncle-grandsire surely is not a true descendant—how unlike your kind!"
idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Uncle, you cannot be a true heir of the house—how unlike your line!"

literal: When about to die he left in the testamentary edict that Jia be Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others to assist government.
idiomatic: On his deathbed he named Jia left vice director, with Prince Xi of Xianyang and others as regents.

literal: Transferred to Governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: Jia became governor of Sizhou.

literal: Jia memorialized asking to build three hundred twenty wards around the capital on four sides, each circuiting twelve hundred paces, begging to levy the three categories of corvée and exempted households to fill this labor.
idiomatic: He asked to ring the capital with three hundred twenty wards of twelve hundred paces each, levying every corvée category to build them.

literal: Though there was temporary toil, treachery and theft would forever cease.
idiomatic: The labor would be brief, he said, but theft would end for good.

literal: An edict followed him.
idiomatic: The edict approved.

literal: Made Guards General, Director of the Masters of Writing, given equal thirds with the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: He became guards general and director of the Masters of Writing with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Jia's consort was granddaughter of Prince Yidu Mu Shou, younger cousin of the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: His consort was granddaughter of Prince Yidu Mu Shou and cousin to the Minister of Works.

literal: An intelligent woman.
idiomatic: She was a clever woman.

literal: When she became Jia's consort she often corrected and aided, brightening the household way.
idiomatic: As Jia's princess she often guided him and brought honor to the house.

literal: Son Shen, style Zhiyuan, inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Shen, style Zhiyuan, inherited the title.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming he was made Inspector of Si.
idiomatic: At Xiaoming's accession he became inspector of Si.

literal: He beforehand practiced grace and trust; the Hu people found it convenient; robbery and banditry ceased.
idiomatic: He ruled with grace beforehand; the Hu were content and banditry stopped.

literal: Later became Inspector of Heng, in the province much accepting bribes, government accomplished by gifts.
idiomatic: Later as inspector of Heng he took endless bribes; office ran on graft.

literal: If a household had a thousand horses he surely took a hundred; this he made constant.
idiomatic: Households with a thousand horses owed him a hundred by custom.

literal: In succession promoted Palace Director of the Masters of Writing, not yet invested.
idiomatic: He was promoted palace director but never received investiture.

literal: For lying with Prince of Chengyang Hui's consort Lady Yu he was sued by Hui in a memorial.
idiomatic: He lay with Prince Hui of Chengyang's consort Lady Yu; Hui sued him.

literal: An edict handed him to the Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yong and other clansmen to decide his crime; he was sent back to his mansion.
idiomatic: The edict sent him to Prince Yong of Gaoyang and kinsmen for judgment; he was sent home.

literal: When the people of Woye garrison Po-lu-ling Pa-ling rebelled, Prince of Huaiyang Yu campaigning against them failed; an edict made Shen Grand Commander of the Northern Route, receiving the direction of Director Li Chong.
idiomatic: When Woye rose under Pa-ling, Prince Yu of Huaiyang failed; Shen was named northern commander under Director Li Chong.

literal: At that time eastern-route commander Cui Xian was defeated at White Way; Shen and the armies retreated to Shuozhou.
idiomatic: Eastern commander Cui Xian lost at White Way; Shen's armies fell back to Shuozhou.

literal: Shen submitted a memorial saying:
idiomatic: Shen memorialized:

literal: Frontier rebels have raised trouble and made disorder; their origin is not of a single morning.
idiomatic: "Border rebels did not arise in a day.

literal: Formerly in Huangshi the shift of garrisons was treated as weighty; they chose kin and worthies, gave banners as commanders, paired them with sons of great houses to die holding the passes.
idiomatic: In Huangshi's day garrison duty was sacred: kinsmen and worthies commanded the passes, noble sons sent to die on the frontier.

literal: Not only was office not abolished—for them even exemptions were granted in full.
idiomatic: They kept office and full tax exemptions.

literal: Men of that time admired and yearned for it.
idiomatic: Men envied the posting.

literal: When the Taihe reign began.
idiomatic: When the Taihe era began,

literal: Vice Director Li Chong held office and managed affairs; Liangzhou natives were all freed from corvée;
idiomatic: Vice Director Li Chong freed Liangzhou natives from corvée

literal: Feng and Pei old clans still guarded the frontier.
idiomatic: while Feng and Pei clans still garrisoned the border.

literal: Unless guilty in their generation none would join them.
idiomatic: None but the disgraced would serve with them.

literal: Campaign garrisons were driven as scouts and runners; a lifetime of promotion did not pass company commander.
idiomatic: Garrison soldiers became scouts and runners; a lifetime might end as company commander.

literal: Yet their former household branches remaining in the capital could obtain upper-grade regular office;
idiomatic: Kin who stayed in the capital won high office;

literal: those at the garrisons were cut off from the clear path.
idiomatic: those at the posts were barred from promotion.

literal: Some fled north to escape demons; many again fled into Hu districts.
idiomatic: Some fled north or into Hu lands.

literal: Then they stiffened the rules on frontier soldiers; garrison men drifting outside were all heard as deserters to be seized by roaming patrols.
idiomatic: Rules tightened; any garrison man abroad was treated as a deserter and seized.

literal: Thus youths could not follow teachers, elders could not seek office.
idiomatic: Youths could not study; elders could not seek office.

literal: Alone made outlaws—those who spoke wept.
idiomatic: They became outcasts, and men wept to speak of it.

literal: From fixing the tripod at Yi and Luo the frontier post grew ever lighter; only the dullest talents went out as garrison generals.
idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang, frontier command grew contemptible; only mediocrities were sent as generals.

literal: Turning to imitate one another they specialized in amassing wealth.
idiomatic: They copied one another and specialized in plunder.

literal: Some were wicked officials from other regions, punished and sent to the frontier, who pointed the way and played with the government offices;
idiomatic: Criminal officials banished to the frontier taught them how to squeeze the government;

literal: government stood on bribes and none could reform themselves.
idiomatic: rule ran on bribes, and none reformed.

literal: All said wicked officials did this—none failed to gnash teeth in added rage.
idiomatic: All blamed such officials and gnashed their teeth.

literal: When Anagui turned traitor and let his plunderers flee, troops were ordered to pursue.
idiomatic: When Anagui betrayed the court and fled, the court sent an army in pursuit.

literal: A hundred fifty thousand men crossed the desert and returned within days.
idiomatic: A hundred fifty thousand crossed the desert and were home again within days.

literal: Frontier men seeing this relief army at once took China lightly in their own minds.
idiomatic: Frontier men saw that army and despised the Middle Kingdom.

literal: Director Li Chong at once reported, asking to change garrisons into provinces; the wish would have been granted—he also foresaw.
idiomatic: Director Li Chong then asked to turn garrisons into provinces; the court would have agreed, and he foresaw the danger.

literal: The court did not permit.
idiomatic: The court refused.

literal: Then the Gaogue garrison commander lost harmony below; Pa-ling killed him in rebellion;
idiomatic: A Gaogue commander lost his men; Pa-ling killed him and rebelled;

literal: besieging cities and seizing land, all he saw he put to death.
idiomatic: wherever he marched he slaughtered.

literal: Imperial armies repeatedly retreated north; rebel bands daily grew.
idiomatic: Imperial armies retreated again and again while rebels swelled.

literal: This campaign was hoped to extinguish and pacify.
idiomatic: This campaign was meant to crush them.

literal: Yet Cui Xian's twin wheels did not return; Chong and your servant hesitated on the road back.
idiomatic: Instead Cui Xian never returned; Chong and I limped back.

literal: Now we together have halted again at Yunzhong.
idiomatic: We halt again at Yunzhong.

literal: Where the horses' heads look we have not yet turned west.
idiomatic: The army will not yet march west.

literal: Officers and soldiers in spirit all lost bone.
idiomatic: Soldiers' hearts are broken.

literal: Today's worry is not only the northwest; I fear every garrison will soon be the same.
idiomatic: The peril is not only the northwest; every garrison may follow.

literal: Affairs under heaven—how easily can they be measured!
idiomatic: Who can measure what comes next under heaven?

literal: At the time they did not adopt his plan.
idiomatic: The court ignored him.

literal: When the eastern and western tribes of the Tiele rebelled, court discussion again recalled Shen's words.
idiomatic: When eastern and western Tiele rebelled, the court remembered Shen's warning.

literal: They sent Concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant Li Daoyuan as grand envoy, wishing again to change garrisons to provinces to follow popular hope.
idiomatic: They sent Li Daoyuan as envoy to turn garrisons into provinces and appease the frontier.

literal: But all six garrisons rebelled; it could not be carried out.
idiomatic: All six garrisons rose before he could act.

literal: Shen later submitted saying: "Now all six garrisons rebel; the two divisions of Gaoche also share their evil party—with weary troops to attack them surely cannot control the enemy.
idiomatic: Shen wrote again: "All six garrisons rebel and both Gaoche divisions join them; weary troops cannot win.

literal: I beg to select troops, or hold the vital point at Heng.
idiomatic: Choose fresh troops or hold Heng's key passes
